speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned persistent vomiting and chest pain; to help me understand your condition better, how long have these symptoms been occurring, and do you have any history of heart disease or recent trauma?

speaker: Patient
text: 51-year-old male. The patient presents to the emergency department with persistent, forceful vomiting after consuming a significant amount of alcohol. His medical history includes recent treatment for Lyme disease with doxycycline. Recently, after a prolonged episode of retching, the patient starts to choke and cough forcefully, experiencing chest pain. The patient appears unable to communicate effectively at this point.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Boerhaave syndrome (spontaneous esophageal rupture). The history of forceful retching following heavy alcohol consumption, followed by the onset of choking, coughing, and chest pain, is classic for this life-threatening condition. I am requesting an emergent CT scan of the chest with oral contrast and a chest X-ray to confirm the diagnosis.
